newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds dip amid French election poll rumours.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds dip amid French election poll rumours.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped undramatically on Wednesday ahead of U.S. data, hit by market rumours of unofficial opinion polls pointing to a left-wing victory in Sunday's second round of the French general election.
"We expect the downward trickle to continue until the afternoon's U.S. data starts coming in, with the main focus on the April durable goods figures," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.27 point from the start at 110.25, yielding 6.43 percent in 1.9 billion crown turnover, while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark fell 0.19 point to 102.77, yielding 6.61 percent.

The 2007's turnover was only 500 million crowns, while the 2006 June future rose 0.18 point to 110.28 with 10 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.13 point to 88.83. The crown traded at a virtually unchanged 3.8087 per mark at 1150 gmt.
The 2006's 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 48 basis points from the start, with the 2007-bund gap also unmoved at 66 bps.
